steps.note: the API built this case's state
Configure an RFQ with line-item awarding so one line can be split across vendors.
Apply the RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Create the single line with the requested total quantity of 10.
Complete the RFQ pricing sheet so the event can be published.
Commit a bidding schedule before publication.
Invite two distinct vendors for the two bids.
Submit the lower bid for the first vendor.
Verify the first vendor bid was accepted.
Submit the second vendor bid at 100.
Verify the second vendor bid was accepted.
Close bidding so awarding is available.
Open the comparison grid containing both bids.

args.goal: On the awarding screen, allocate 6 units to the vendor with the 90 bid and 4 units to the vendor with the 100 bid, verify Awarded Vendors reads 2/2 and the allocation totals 10 units, create the proposal, fill all required proposal fields, submit it, and stop on the proposal page showing the split values 6 × 90 = 540, 4 × 100 = 400, and total 940

steps.note: No catalog assertion can enter two vendor quantities or verify the split arithmetic while creating the proposal, so perform and verify those buyer-side actions directly.
Confirm the submitted proposal is awaiting approval before the approver acts.

args.need: sign in as the approver, open this proposal from Approvals, enter the remark "OK — QA", approve it, and return to the buyer view

steps.note: The approver is a separate account and the catalog cannot perform that login or approval.

args.goal: After approval, inspect the buyer's resulting order records and verify that the awarded bids are selected, exactly one purchase order exists for each awarded vendor, and the event is in the History list

steps.note: The catalog has no assertion that directly reads post-approval vendor-specific PO creation, so inspect the resulting buyer screens after the approver completes the action.
